                available_excerpt: '# Known Facts


                  - Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15 (~10
                  weeks out).

                  - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts
                  into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account
                  and balance and full access to Mosaic''s product set.

                  - Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC''d by
                  Harbor.

                  - Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states; Mosaic
                  Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four new
                  markets.

                  - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; Mosaic
                  has pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying documents
                  for users onboarded before 2023.

                  - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
                  terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction feed
                  at Mosaic''s engine on day 1.

                  - Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on first
                  transfer, launching close+1.

                  - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from
                  the last year at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.

                  - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts
                  into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account
                  and balance.

                  - Plan is no re-verification of Harbor''s existing KYC; Harbor users
                  were already KYC''d.

                  - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail
                  results exist for everyone but underlying documents are missing
                  for users onboarded before 2023.

                  - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
                  terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction feed to
                  Mosaic Relay''s engine on day 1.

                  - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from
                  the last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.

                  - How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase
                  (Mosaic buys Harbor''s assets)

                  - Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program currently permit relying
                  on another institution''s prior KYC without re-verification, or
                  is re-verification required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance

                  - What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs from
                  the last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence

                  - For the four new markets opened by the combined footprint, does
                  Mosaic Relay plan to operate under Harbor''s existing licenses or
                  apply for its own? — Use/assume Harbor''s licenses

                  - For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents,
                  what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML customer
                  identification and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet known
                  whether Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor''s
                  prior KYC; compliance must confirm.

                  - Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last
                  year been reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open alerts
                  and SAR history have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.

                  - For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint,
                  what is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval
                  before onboarding those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans
                  to use or assume Harbor''s licenses for the four new markets.


                  ## Assumptions


                  - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s existing money transmission licenses
                  and Harbor''s MTLs are transferable or can be maintained through
                  the acquisition without new state approval

                  - [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy
                  Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations without the underlying
                  documents

                  - [Assumption] The transaction monitoring repoint can be completed
                  and validated before close without a monitoring gap

                  - [Assumption] Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject
                  to state MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).

                  - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter
                  in 41 states (per the request).

                  - [Assumption] The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock
                  purchase, which affects whether Harbor''s licenses and SAR/alert
                  obligations transfer (structure not yet confirmed).

                  '

                  text: '# Known Facts


                    - Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15
                    (~10 weeks out).

                    - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts
                    into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified
                    account and balance and full access to Mosaic''s product set.

                    - Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC''d
                    by Harbor.

                    - Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states;
                    Mosaic Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening
                    four new markets.

                    - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; Mosaic
                    has pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying documents
                    for users onboarded before 2023.

                    - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose
                    contract terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction
                    feed at Mosaic''s engine on day 1.

                    - Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on first
                    transfer, launching close+1.

                    - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs
                    from the last year at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.

                    - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts
                    into Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified
                    account and balance.

                    - Plan is no re-verification of Harbor''s existing KYC; Harbor
                    users were already KYC''d.

                    - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail
                    results exist for everyone but underlying documents are missing
                    for users onboarded before 2023.

                    - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose
                    contract terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction
                    feed to Mosaic Relay''s engine on day 1.

                    - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs
                    from the last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.

                    - How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase
                    (Mosaic buys Harbor''s assets)

                    - Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program currently permit relying
                    on another institution''s prior KYC without re-verification, or
                    is re-verification required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance

                    - What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs from
                    the last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence

                    - For the four new markets opened by the combined footprint, does
                    Mosaic Relay plan to operate under Harbor''s existing licenses
                    or apply for its own? — Use/assume Harbor''s licenses

                    - For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents,
                    what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML customer
                    identification and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet
                    known whether Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program permits reliance
                    on Harbor''s prior KYC; compliance must confirm.

                    - Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last
                    year been reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open alerts
                    and SAR history have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.

                    - For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint,
                    what is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval
                    before onboarding those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans
                    to use or assume Harbor''s licenses for the four new markets.


                    ## Assumptions


                    - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s existing money transmission licenses
                    and Harbor''s MTLs are transferable or can be maintained through
                    the acquisition without new state approval

                    - [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy
                    Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations without the underlying
                    documents

                    - [Assumption] The transaction monitoring repoint can be completed
                    and validated before close without a monitoring gap

                    - [Assumption] Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject
                    to state MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet
                    confirmed).

                    - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter
                    in 41 states (per the request).

                    - [Assumption] The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock
                    purchase, which affects whether Harbor''s licenses and SAR/alert
                    obligations transfer (structure not yet confirmed).

                    '

      view_version: 3
      base_position: '## Working position


        The Harbor Pay migration needs legal and compliance review before the planned
        close. The leading concern is that an asset purchase generally requires Mosaic
        Relay to confirm its own authority to operate in each state; the current plan
        to use or assume Harbor''s licenses is not established as legally effective.


        The second concern is BSA/AML readiness. Mosaic Relay has not confirmed whether
        its AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC, and underlying
        records are missing for some pre-2023 users. Harbor''s open alerts and SAR
        history also remain unread. These gaps make a day-one migration without re-verification
        or account restrictions difficult to support.


        Transaction monitoring continuity is also material because Harbor''s vendor
        ends at close. The repointed feed should be tested and validated before migrated
        users receive full access. The $50 bonus is lower priority but still needs
        review once its eligibility, funding, terms, and disclosures are known.


        ## Plausible alternatives


        A narrower launch could exclude the four new markets, restrict users whose
        KYC evidence is incomplete, or delay full product access until alert review
        and monitoring validation finish. A full day-one launch remains possible only
        if state licensing, AML/CIP reliance, alert handling, and monitoring continuity
        are confirmed.


        ## Material facts and assumptions


        Reported facts include the asset-purchase structure, the current plan to rely
        on Harbor''s licenses, the lack of a compliance answer on KYC reliance, and
        the unread alerts and SAR history. The analysis assumes both entities conduct
        regulated money-transmission activity and that Mosaic Relay will become the
        operating provider immediately after close. It does not assume that Harbor''s
        licenses transfer or that Harbor''s KYC is sufficient.


        ## What could change this view


        The view could change if state counsel confirms an effective licensing path
        for each affected state, compliance confirms permissible reliance with adequate
        records or remediation, diligence clears the alerts and SAR history, and testing
        shows no monitoring gap. The bonus structure remains unknown.


        ## Support limit


        This is generated analysis based on reported matter facts. No external authority
        was retrieved.'

            available_excerpt: '# Original Request


              From: Dana, PM — Growth & Integration

              Subject: Harbor migration — anything here need legal?


              We''re acquiring Harbor Pay. Close is targeted Nov 15 (~10 weeks). Migration
              plan:


              240k consumer users, 12k business accounts move into our app on day
              1 post-close. One unified account, one balance, full access to our product
              set.

              No re-verification — they were already KYC''d by Harbor.

              Harbor holds MTLs in 38 states, we hold 41. Combined that''s 44 — nice
              win, opens four new markets.

              Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024. We have pass/fail
              results for everyone, but not the underlying documents for users onboarded
              before 2023.

              Harbor''s monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract terminates
              at close. Plan is to repoint their transaction feed at our engine on
              day 1.

              Marketing wants a "Welcome" campaign with a $50 bonus on first transfer,
              launching close+1.

              Diligence flagged that Harbor has ~40 open alerts and "a handful" of
              SARs from the last year. Nobody''s read them yet.


              Does any of this need legal before close? It''s really just a data migration.

              '

                From: Dana, PM — Growth & Integration

                Subject: Harbor migration — anything here need legal?


                We''re acquiring Harbor Pay. Close is targeted Nov 15 (~10 weeks).
                Migration plan:


                240k consumer users, 12k business accounts move into our app on day
                1 post-close. One unified account, one balance, full access to our
                product set.

                No re-verification — they were already KYC''d by Harbor.

                Harbor holds MTLs in 38 states, we hold 41. Combined that''s 44 —
                nice win, opens four new markets.

                Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024. We have
                pass/fail results for everyone, but not the underlying documents for

                Harbor''s monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract terminates
                at close. Plan is to repoint their transaction feed at our engine
                on day 1.

                Marketing wants a "Welcome" campaign with a $50 bonus on first transfer,
                launching close+1.

                Diligence flagged that Harbor has ~40 open alerts and "a handful"
                of SARs from the last year. Nobody''s read them yet.


                Does any of this need legal before close? It''s really just a data
                migration.

                '

                Title 31—Money and Finance: Treasury


                Subtitle B—Regulations Relating to Money and Finance


                CHAPTER X—FINANCIAL CRIMES ENFORCEMENT NETWORK, DEPARTMENT OF THE
                TREASURY


                PART 1022—RULES FOR MONEY SERVICES BUSINESSES


                Subpart B—Programs


                § 1022.210 Anti-money laundering programs for money services businesses.


                31 CFR § 1022.210 - Anti-money laundering programs for money services
                businesses.


                CFR


                prev | next


                § 1022.210 Anti-money laundering programs for money services businesses.


                (a) Each money services business, as defined by § 1010.100(ff) of
                this chapter, shall develop, implement, and maintain an effective
                anti-money laundering program. An effective anti-money laundering
                program is one that is reasonably designed to prevent the money services
                business from being used to facilitate money laundering and the financing
                of terrorist activities.


                (b) The program shall be commensurate with the risks posed by the
                location and size of, and the nature and volume of the financial services
                provided by, the money services business.


                (c) The program shall be in writing, and a money services business
                shall make copies of the anti-money laundering program available for
                inspection to the Department of the Treasury upon request.


                (d) At a minimum, the program shall:


                (1) Incorporate policies, procedures, and internal controls reasonably
                designed to assure compliance with this chapter.


                (i) Policies, procedures, and internal controls developed and implemented
                under this section shall include provisions for complying with the
                requirements of this chapter including, to the extent applicable to
                the money services business, requirements for:


                (A) Verifying customer identification, including as set forth in paragraph
                (d)(1)(iv) of this section;


                (B) Filing Reports;


                (C) Creating and retaining records;


                (D) Responding to law enforcement requests.


                (ii) Money services businesses that have automated data processing
                systems should integrate their compliance procedures with such systems.


                (iii) A person that is a money services business solely because it
                is an agent for another money services business as set forth in §
                1022.380(a)(3) , and the money services business for which it serves
                as agent, may by agreement allocate between them responsibility for
                development of policies, procedures, and internal controls required
                by this paragraph (d)(1). Each money services business shall remain
                solely responsible for implementation of the requirements set forth
                in this section, and nothing in this paragraph (d)(1) relieves any
                money services business from its obligation to establish and maintain
                an effective anti-money laundering program.


                (iv) A money services business that is a provider or seller of prepaid
                access must establish procedures to verify the identity of a person
                who obtains prepaid access under a prepaid program and obtain identifying
                information concerning such a person , including name, date of birth,
                address, and identification number. Sellers of prepaid access must
                also establish procedures to verify the identity of a person who obtains
                prepaid access to funds that exceed $10,000 during any one day and
                obtain identifying information concerning such a person , including
                name, date of birth, address, and identification number. Providers
                of prepaid access must retain access to such identifying information
                for five years after the last use of the prepaid access device or
                vehicle; such information obtained by sellers of prepaid access must
                be retained for five years from the date of the sale of the prepaid
                access device or vehicle.


                (2) Designate a person to assure day to day compliance with the program
                and this chapter. The responsibilities of such person shall include
                assuring that:


                (i) The money services business properly files reports, and creates
                and retains records, in accordance with applicable requirements of
                this chapter;


                (ii) The compliance program is updated as necessary to reflect current
                requirements of this chapter, and related guidance issued by the Department
                of the Treasury ; and


                (iii) The money services business provides appropriate training and
                education in accordance with paragraph (d)(3) of this section.


                (3) Provide education and/or training of appropriate personnel concerning
                their responsibilities under the program, including training in the
                detection of suspicious transactions to the extent that the money
                services business is required to report such transactions under this
                chapter.


                (4) Provide for independent review to monitor and maintain an adequate
                program. The scope and frequency of the review shall be commensurate
                with the risk of the financial services provided by the money services
                business. Such review may be conducted by an officer or employee of
                the money services business so long as the reviewer is not the person
                designated in paragraph (d)(2) of this section.'

              to the Department of the Treasury upon request.


              (d) At a minimum, the program shall:


              (1) Incorporate policies, procedures, and internal controls reasonably
              designed to assure compliance with this chapter.


              (i) Policies, procedures, and internal controls developed and implemented
              under this section shall include provisions for complying with the requirements
              of this chapter including, to the extent applicable to the money services
              business, requirements for:


              (A) Verifying customer identification, including as set forth in paragraph
              (d)(1)(iv) of this section;


              (B) Filing Reports;


              (C) Creating and retaining records;


              (D) Responding to law enforcement requests.


              (ii) Money services businesses that have automated data processing systems
              should integrate their compliance procedures with such systems.


              (iii) A person that is a money services business solely because it is
              an agent for another money services business as set forth in § 1022.380(a)(3)
              , and the money services business for which it serves as agent, may
              by agreement allocate between them responsibility for development of
              policies, procedures, and internal controls required by this paragraph
              (d)(1). Each money services business shall remain solely responsible
              for implementation of the requirements set forth in this section, and
              nothing in this paragraph (d)(1) relieves any money services business
              from its obligation to establish and maintain an effective anti-money
              laundering program.


              (iv) A money services business that is a provider or seller of prepaid
              access must establish procedures to verify the identity of a person
              who obtains prepaid access under a prepaid program and obtain identifying
              information concerning such a person , including name, date of birth,
              address, and identification number. Sellers of prepaid access must also
              establish procedures to verify the identity of a person who obtains
              prepaid access to funds that exceed $10,000 during any one day and obtain
              identifying information concerning such a person , including name, date
              of birth, address, and identification number. Providers of prepaid access
              must retain access to such identifying information for five years after
              the last use of the prepaid access device or vehicle; such information
              obtained by sellers of prepaid access must be retained for five years
              from the date of the sale of the prepaid access device or vehicle.


              (2) Designate a person to assure day to day compliance with the program
              and this chapter. The responsibilities of such person shall include
              assuring that:


              (i) The money services business properly files reports, and creates
              and retains records, in accordance with applicable requirements of this
              chapter;


              (ii) The compliance program is updated as necessary to reflect current
              requirements of this chapter, and related guidance issued by the Department
              of the Treasury ; and


              (iii) The money services business provides appropriate training and
              education in accordance with paragraph (d)(3) of this section.


              (3) Provide education and/or training of appropriate personnel concerning
              their responsibilities under the program, including training in the
              detection of suspicious transactions to the extent that the money services
              business is required to report such transactions under this chapter.


              (4) Provide for independent review to monitor and maintain an adequate
              program. The scope and frequency of the review shall be commensurate
              with the risk of the financial services provided by the money services
              business. Such review may be conducted by an officer or employee of
              the money services business so long as the reviewer is not the person
              designated in paragraph (d)(2) of this section.'

                Title 31—Money and Finance: Treasury


                Subtitle B—Regulations Relating to Money and Finance


                CHAPTER X—FINANCIAL CRIMES ENFORCEMENT NETWORK, DEPARTMENT OF THE
                TREASURY


                PART 1022—RULES FOR MONEY SERVICES BUSINESSES


                Subpart C—Reports Required To Be Made By Money Services Businesses


                § 1022.320 Reports by money services businesses of suspicious transactions.


                31 CFR § 1022.320 - Reports by money services businesses of suspicious
                transactions.


                CFR


                Table of Popular Names


                prev | next


                § 1022.320 Reports by money services businesses of suspicious transactions.


                (a)  General.


                (1) Every money services business described in § 1010.100(ff)(1) ,
                (3), (4), (5), (6), and (7) of this chapter, shall file with the Treasury
                Department, to the extent and in the manner required by this section,
                a report of any suspicious transaction relevant to a possible violation
                of law or regulation. Any money services business may also file with
                the Treasury Department, by using the form specified in paragraph
                (b)(1) of this section, or otherwise, a report of any suspicious transaction
                that it believes is relevant to the possible violation of any law
                or regulation but whose reporting is not required by this section.


                (2) A transaction requires reporting under the terms of this section
                if it is conducted or attempted by, at, or through a money services
                business, involves or aggregates funds or other assets of at least
                $2,000 (except as provided in paragraph (a)(3) of this section), and
                the money services business knows, suspects, or has reason to suspect
                that the transaction (or a pattern of transactions of which the transaction
                is a part):


                (i) Involves funds derived from illegal activity or is intended or
                conducted in order to hide or disguise funds or assets derived from
                illegal activity (including, without limitation, the ownership, nature,
                source, location, or control of such funds or assets) as part of a
                plan to violate or evade any Federal law or regulation or to avoid
                any transaction reporting requirement under Federal law or regulation;


                (ii) Is designed, whether through structuring or other means, to evade
                any requirements of this chapter or of any other regulations promulgated
                under the Bank Secrecy Act ; or


                (iii) Serves no business or apparent lawful purpose, and the reporting
                money services business knows of no reasonable explanation for the
                transaction after examining the available facts, including the background
                and possible purpose of the transaction .


                (iv) Involves use of the money services business to facilitate criminal
                activity.


                (3) To the extent that the identification of transactions required
                to be reported is derived from a review of clearance records or other
                similar records of money orders or traveler''s checks that have been
                sold or processed, an issuer of money orders or traveler''s checks
                shall only be required to report a transaction or pattern of transactions
                that involves or aggregates funds or other assets of at least $5,000.


                (4) The obligation to identify and properly and timely to report a
                suspicious transaction rests with each money services business involved
                in the transaction , provided that no more than one report is required
                to be filed by the money services businesses involved in a particular
                transaction (so long as the report filed contains all relevant facts).
                Whether, in addition to any liability on its own for failure to report,
                a money services business that issues the instrument or provides the
                funds transfer service involved in the transaction may be liable for
                the failure of another money services business involved in the transaction
                to report that transaction depends upon the nature of the contractual
                or other relationship between the businesses, and the legal effect
                of the facts and circumstances of the relationship and transaction
                involved, under general principles of the law of agency.


                (b)  Filing procedures —(1) What to file. A suspicious transaction
                shall be reported by completing a Suspicious Activity Report(“SAR”),
                and collecting and maintaining supporting documentation as required
                by paragraph (c) of this section.


                (2)  Where to file. The SAR shall be filed in a central location to
                be determined by FinCEN , as indicated in the instructions to the
                SAR.'

                Title 31—Money and Finance: Treasury


                Subtitle B—Regulations Relating to Money and Finance


                CHAPTER X—FINANCIAL CRIMES ENFORCEMENT NETWORK, DEPARTMENT OF THE
                TREASURY


                PART 1010—GENERAL PROVISIONS


                Subpart D—Records Required To Be Maintained


                § 1010.430 Nature of records and retention period.


                31 CFR § 1010.430 - Nature of records and retention period.


                CFR


                prev | next


                § 1010.430 Nature of records and retention period.


                (a) Wherever it is required that there be retained either the original
                or a copy or reproduction of a check, draft, monetary instrument ,
                investment security , or other similar instrument, there shall be
                retained a copy of both front and back of each such instrument or
                document, except that no copy need be retained of the back of any
                instrument or document which is entirely blank or which contains only
                standardized printed information, a copy of which is on file.


                (b) Records required by this chapter to be retained by financial institutions
                may be those made in the ordinary course of business by a financial
                institution . If no record is made in the ordinary course of business
                of any transaction with respect to which records are required to be
                retained by this chapter, then such a record shall be prepared in
                writing by the financial institution .


                (c) The rules and regulations issued by the Internal Revenue Service
                under 26 U.S.C. 6109 determine what constitutes a taxpayer identification
                number and whose number shall be obtained in the case of an account
                maintained by one or more persons.


                (d) All records that are required to be retained by this chapter shall
                be retained for a period of five years. Records or reports required
                to be kept pursuant to an order issued under § 1010.370 of this chapter
                shall be retained for the period of time specified in such order,
                not to exceed five years. All such records shall be filed or stored
                in such a way as to be accessible within a reasonable period of time,
                taking into consideration the nature of the record, and the amount
                of time expired since the record was made.


                [ 75 FR 65812 , Oct. 26, 2010, as amended at 81 FR 76864 , Nov. 4,
                2016]

            available_excerpt: '# Known Facts


              - Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15 (~10 weeks
              out).

              - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into
              Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and
              balance and full access to Mosaic''s product set.

              - Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC''d by Harbor.

              - Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states; Mosaic
              Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four new markets.

              - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; Mosaic
              has pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying documents
              for users onboarded before 2023.

              - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
              terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction feed at
              Mosaic''s engine on day 1.

              - Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on first transfer,
              launching close+1.

              - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from the
              last year at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.

              - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into
              Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and
              balance.

              - Plan is no re-verification of Harbor''s existing KYC; Harbor users
              were already KYC''d.

              - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail
              results exist for everyone but underlying documents are missing for
              users onboarded before 2023.

              - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
              terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction feed to Mosaic
              Relay''s engine on day 1.

              - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from the
              last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.

              - How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase (Mosaic
              buys Harbor''s assets)

              - Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program currently permit relying on another
              institution''s prior KYC without re-verification, or is re-verification
              required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance

              - What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs from the
              last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence

              - For the four new markets opened by the combined footprint, does Mosaic
              Relay plan to operate under Harbor''s existing licenses or apply for
              its own? — Use/assume Harbor''s licenses

              - For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents, what
              is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML customer identification
              and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet known whether Mosaic
              Relay''s AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC; compliance
              must confirm.

              - Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last year
              been reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open alerts and SAR history
              have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.

              - For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint,
              what is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval
              before onboarding those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans to
              use or assume Harbor''s licenses for the four new markets.


              ## Assumptions


              - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s existing money transmission licenses
              and Harbor''s MTLs are transferable or can be maintained through the
              acquisition without new state approval

              - [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy Mosaic
              Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations without the underlying documents

              - [Assumption] The transaction monitoring repoint can be completed and
              validated before close without a monitoring gap

              - [Assumption] Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject to
              state MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).

              - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter in
              41 states (per the request).

              - [Assumption] The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock purchase,
              which affects whether Harbor''s licenses and SAR/alert obligations transfer
              (structure not yet confirmed).

              '

                Title 31—Money and Finance: Treasury


                Subtitle B—Regulations Relating to Money and Finance


                CHAPTER X—FINANCIAL CRIMES ENFORCEMENT NETWORK, DEPARTMENT OF THE
                TREASURY


                PART 1022—RULES FOR MONEY SERVICES BUSINESSES


                Subpart C—Reports Required To Be Made By Money Services Businesses


                § 1022.320 Reports by money services businesses of suspicious transactions.


                31 CFR § 1022.320 - Reports by money services businesses of suspicious
                transactions.


                CFR


                Table of Popular Names


                prev | next


                § 1022.320 Reports by money services businesses of suspicious transactions.


                (a)  General.


                (1) Every money services business described in § 1010.100(ff)(1) ,
                (3), (4), (5), (6), and (7) of this chapter, shall file with the Treasury
                Department, to the extent and in the manner required by this section,
                a report of any suspicious transaction relevant to a possible violation
                of law or regulation. Any money services business may also file with
                the Treasury Department, by using the form specified in paragraph
                (b)(1) of this section, or otherwise, a report of any suspicious transaction
                that it believes is relevant to the possible violation of any law
                or regulation but whose reporting is not required by this section.


                (2) A transaction requires reporting under the terms of this section
                if it is conducted or attempted by, at, or through a money services
                business, involves or aggregates funds or other assets of at least
                $2,000 (except as provided in paragraph (a)(3) of this section), and
                the money services business knows, suspects, or has reason to suspect
                that the transaction (or a pattern of transactions of which the transaction
                is a part):


                (i) Involves funds derived from illegal activity or is intended or
                conducted in order to hide or disguise funds or assets derived from
                illegal activity (including, without limitation, the ownership, nature,
                source, location, or control of such funds or assets) as part of a
                plan to violate or evade any Federal law or regulation or to avoid
                any transaction reporting requirement under Federal law or regulation;


                (ii) Is designed, whether through structuring or other means, to evade
                any requirements of this chapter or of any other regulations promulgated
                under the Bank Secrecy Act ; or


                (iii) Serves no business or apparent lawful purpose, and the reporting
                money services business knows of no reasonable explanation for the
                transaction after examining the available facts, including the background
                and possible purpose of the transaction .


                (iv) Involves use of the money services business to facilitate criminal
                activity.


                (3) To the extent that the identification of transactions required
                to be reported is derived from a review of clearance records or other
                similar records of money orders or traveler''s checks that have been
                sold or processed, an issuer of money orders or traveler''s checks
                shall only be required to report a transaction or pattern of transactions
                that involves or aggregates funds or other assets of at least $5,000.


                (4) The obligation to identify and properly and timely to report a
                suspicious transaction rests with each money services business involved
                in the transaction , provided that no more than one report is required
                to be filed by the money services businesses involved in a particular
                transaction (so long as the report filed contains all relevant facts).
                Whether, in addition to any liability on its own for failure to report,
                a money services business that issues the instrument or provides the
                funds transfer service involved in the transaction may be liable for
                the failure of another money services business involved in the transaction
                to report that transaction depends upon the nature of the contractual
                or other relationship between the businesses, and the legal effect
                of the facts and circumstances of the relationship and transaction
                involved, under general principles of the law of agency.


                (b)  Filing procedures —(1) What to file. A suspicious transaction
                shall be reported by completing a Suspicious Activity Report(“SAR”),
                and collecting and maintaining supporting documentation as required
                by paragraph (c) of this section.


                (2)  Where to file. The SAR shall be filed in a central location to
                be determined by FinCEN , as indicated in the instructions to the
                SAR.'

              Title 31—Money and Finance: Treasury


              Subtitle B—Regulations Relating to Money and Finance


              CHAPTER X—FINANCIAL CRIMES ENFORCEMENT NETWORK, DEPARTMENT OF THE TREASURY


              PART 1022—RULES FOR MONEY SERVICES BUSINESSES


              Subpart C—Reports Required To Be Made By Money Services Businesses


              § 1022.320 Reports by money services businesses of suspicious transactions.


              31 CFR § 1022.320 - Reports by money services businesses of suspicious
              transactions.


              CFR


              Table of Popular Names


              prev | next


              § 1022.320 Reports by money services businesses of suspicious transactions.


              (a)  General.


              (1) Every money services business described in § 1010.100(ff)(1) , (3),
              (4), (5), (6), and (7) of this chapter, shall file with the Treasury
              Department, to the extent and in the manner required by this section,
              a report of any suspicious transaction relevant to a possible violation
              of law or regulation. Any money services business may also file with
              the Treasury Department, by using the form specified in paragraph (b)(1)
              of this section, or otherwise, a report of any suspicious transaction
              that it believes is relevant to the possible violation of any law or
              regulation but whose reporting is not required by this section.


              (2) A transaction requires reporting under the terms of this section
              if it is conducted or attempted by, at, or through a money services
              business, involves or aggregates funds or other assets of at least $2,000
              (except as provided in paragraph (a)(3) of this section), and the money
              services business knows, suspects, or has reason to suspect that the
              transaction (or a pattern of transactions of which the transaction is
              a part):


              (i) Involves funds derived from illegal activity or is intended or conducted
              in order to hide or disguise funds or assets derived from illegal activity
              (including, without limitation, the ownership, nature, source, location,
              or control of such funds or assets) as part of a plan to violate or
              evade any Federal law or regulation or to avoid any transaction reporting
              requirement under Federal law or regulation;


              (ii) Is designed, whether through structuring or other means, to evade
              any requirements of this chapter or of any other regulations promulgated
              under the Bank Secrecy Act ; or


              (iii) Serves no business or apparent lawful purpose, and the reporting
              money services business knows of no reasonable explanation for the transaction
              after examining the available facts, including the background and possible
              purpose of the transaction .


              (iv) Involves use of the money services business to facilitate criminal
              activity.


              (3) To the extent that the identification of transactions required to
              be reported is derived from a review of clearance records or other similar
              records of money orders or traveler''s checks that have been sold or
              processed, an issuer of money orders or traveler''s checks shall only
              be required to report a transaction or pattern of transactions that
              involves or aggregates funds or other assets of at least $5,000.


              (4) The obligation to identify and properly and timely to report a suspicious
              transaction rests with each money services business involved in the
              transaction , provided that no more than one report is required to be
              filed by the money services businesses involved in a particular transaction
              (so long as the report filed contains all relevant facts). Whether,
              in addition to any liability on its own for failure to report, a money
              services business that issues the instrument or provides the funds transfer
              service involved in the transaction may be liable for the failure of
              another money services business involved in the transaction to report
              that transaction depends upon the nature of the contractual or other
              relationship between the businesses, and the legal effect of the facts
              and circumstances of the relationship and transaction involved, under
              general principles of the law of agency.


              (b)  Filing procedures —(1) What to file. A suspicious transaction shall
              be reported by completing a Suspicious Activity Report(“SAR”), and collecting
              and maintaining supporting documentation as required by paragraph (c)
              of this section.


              (2)  Where to file. The SAR shall be filed in a central location to
              be determined by FinCEN , as indicated in the instructions to the SAR.'

            extraction_state: complete
            selected_passages:
            - unit_id: p000014
              start: 0
              end: 1963
              page_number: 14
              section_label: null
              body_hash: 5b5d2f6c388b9bcf98252d205bb001dbdce26951229e0e6896dfecf0358be545
              path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000014.md
              text: "14 \n \nARTICLE V \nMoney Transmission Licenses \nSection 5.01
                License Required. \n(a) \nA person may not engage in the business
                of money transmission or \nadvertise, solicit, or hold itself out
                as providing money transmission unless the person is licensed \nunder
                this [Act]; \n(b) \n[Section 5.01(a)] does not apply to: \n(1) \nA
                person that is an authorized delegate of a person licensed under \nthis
                [Act] acting within the scope of authority conferred by a written
                contract with the \nlicensee; or \n(2) \nA person that is exempt pursuant
                to [Section 3.01] and does not \nengage in money transmission outside
                the scope of such exemption. \n(c) \nA license issued under [Section
                5.05] is not transferable or assignable. \nSection 5.02 Consistent
                State Licensing. \n(a) \nTo establish consistent licensing between
                [this state] and other states, the \n[Commissioner] is authorized
                and encouraged to: \n(1) \nimplement all licensing provisions of this
                [Act] in a manner that is \nconsistent with other states that have
                adopted this [Act]or multistate licensing processes; \nand \n(2) \nparticipate
                in nationwide protocols for licensing cooperation and \ncoordination
                among state regulators provided that such protocols are consistent
                with this \n[Act]. \n(b) \nIn order to fulfill the purposes of this
                [Act], the [Commissioner] is \nauthorized and encouraged to establish
                relationships or contracts with NMLS or other entities \ndesignated
                by NMLS to enable the [Commissioner] to: \n(1) \ncollect and maintain
                records; \n(2) \ncoordinate multistate licensing processes and supervision
                processes; \n(3) \nprocess fees; and \n(4) \nfacilitate communication
                between [state] and licensees or other \npersons subject to this [Act].
                \n(c) \nThe [Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged to utilize
                NMLS for all \naspects of licensing in accordance with this [Act],
                including but not limited to, license applications, \napplications
                for acquisitions of control, surety bonds, reporting, criminal history
                background\n"

              acting within the scope of authority conferred by a written contract
              with the \nlicensee; or \n(2) \nA person that is exempt pursuant to
              [Section 3.01] and does not \nengage in money transmission outside the
              scope of such exemption. \n(c) \nA license issued under [Section 5.05]
              is not transferable or assignable. \nSection 5.02 Consistent State Licensing.
              \n(a) \nTo establish consistent licensing between [this state] and other
              states, the \n[Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged to: \n(1)
              \nimplement all licensing provisions of this [Act] in a manner that
              is \nconsistent with other states that have adopted this [Act]or multistate

              and \n(4) \nfacilitate communication between [state] and licensees or

              authorized and encouraged to utilize NMLS for all \naspects of licensing
              in accordance with this [Act], including but not limited to, license

            - unit_id: p000022

              page_number: 22
              section_label: null
              body_hash: 175b57e812c71a8532569030d2db7113b5adc94e61bd9922dc0fee5d833c2748
              path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000022.md
              text: "22 \n \n(e) \nWhen an application for acquisition of control
                under this [Section 6.01] \nappears to include all the items and address
                all of the matters that are required, the application shall \nbe considered
                complete and the [Commissioner] shall promptly notify the applicant
                in a record of \nthe date on which the application was determined
                to be complete and:15 \n \n(1) \nThe [Commissioner] shall approve
                or deny the application within 60 \ndays after the completion date;
                or \n(2) \nif the application is not approved or denied within 60
                days after the \ncompletion date: \n(A) \nthe application is approved;
                and \n(B) \nthe person, or group of persons acting in concert, are
                not \nprohibited from acquiring control. \n(3) \nThe [Commissioner]
                may for good cause extend the application \nperiod. \n(f) \nA determination
                by the [Commissioner] that an application is complete and \nis accepted
                for processing means only that the application, on its face, appears
                to include all of the \nitems and address all of the matters that
                are required, and is not an assessment of the substance of \nthe application
                or of the sufficiency of the information provided. \n(g) \nWhen an
                application is filed and considered complete under [Section \n6.01(e)],
                the [Commissioner] shall investigate the financial condition and responsibility,
                financial \nand business experience, character, and general fitness
                of the person, or group of persons acting in \nconcert, seeking to
                acquire control. The [Commissioner] shall approve an acquisition of
                control \npursuant to this [Section 6.01] if the [Commissioner] finds
                that all of the following conditions have \nbeen fulfilled: \n(1)
                \nThe requirements of subsections (b) and (d) have been met, as \napplicable;
                and \n(2) \nthe financial condition and responsibility, financial
                and business \nexperience, competence, character, and general fitness
                of the person, or group of persons \nacting in concert, seeking to
                acquire control; and the competence, experience, character, \nand
                general fitness of the key individuals and persons that would be in
                control of the \nlicensee after the acquisition of control indicate
                that it is in the interest of the public to \npermit the person, or
                group of persons acting in concert, to control the licensee. \n(h)
                \nIf an applicant avails itself or is otherwise subject to a multistate
                licensing \n \n15 Commentary: NMLS will accommodate and streamline
                the process of communicating when applications are \nreceived and
                when states consider them to have been complete. The intent of this
                Act is for the application period to \nbegin on the day an application
                is determined to be complete.\n"

              page_number: 23
              section_label: null
              body_hash: 83a664c778fbc9de0b4d13270e2a918f6488b461db1a6617e3d36032163068ca
              path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000023.md
              text: "23 \n \nprocess: \n(1) \nthe [Commissioner] is authorized and
                encouraged to accept the \ninvestigation results of a lead investigative
                state for the purpose of [Section 6.01(g)] if the \nlead investigative
                state has sufficient staffing, expertise, and minimum standards; or
                \n(2) \nif [state] is a lead investigative state, the [Commissioner]
                is \nauthorized and encouraged to investigate the applicant pursuant
                to [Section 6.01(g)] and \nthe timeframes established by agreement
                through the multistate licensing process. \n(i) \nThe [Commissioner]
                shall issue a formal written notice of the denial of an \napplication
                to acquire control within thirty (30) days of the decision to deny
                the application. The \n[Commissioner] shall set forth in the notice
                of denial the specific reasons for the denial of the \napplication.
                An applicant whose application is denied by the [Commissioner] under
                this [Section \n6.01(i)] may appeal within thirty (30) days16 after
                receipt of the written notice of the denial \n[pursuant to state administrative
                law procedures]. \n(j) \nThe requirements of [Section 6.01(a) and
                (b)] do not apply to any of the \nfollowing: \n(1) \nA person that
                acts as a proxy for the sole purpose of voting at a \ndesignated meeting
                of the shareholders or holders of voting shares or voting interests
                of a \nlicensee or a person in control of a licensee; \n(2) \nA person
                that acquires control of a licensee by devise or descent; \n(3) \nA
                person that acquires control of a licensee as a personal \nrepresentative,
                custodian, guardian, conservator, or trustee, or as an officer appointed
                by a \ncourt of competent jurisdiction or by operation of law; \n(4)
                \nA person that is exempt under [Section 3.01(g)]; \n(5) \nA person
                that the [Commissioner] determines is not subject to \n[Section 6.01(a)]
                based on the public interest; \n(6) \nA public offering of securities
                of a licensee or a person in control of \na licensee; or \n(7) \nAn
                internal reorganization of a person in control of the licensee \nwhere
                the ultimate person in control of the licensee remains the same. \n(k)
                \nPersons in [Sections 6.01(j)(2), (3), (4), (6), (7)] in cooperation
                with the \nlicensee shall notify the [Commissioner] within [15] days
                after the acquisition of control.17 \n \n16 Commentary: Administrative
                procedures for challenging a departmental decision may be derived
                from other \naspects of state law. In such a case, this Act should
                be adjusted to reflect the relevant administrative process. \n17 Commentary:
                Notice is satisfied upon updating the licensee’s NMLS record.\n"

              text: "24 \n \n(l) \nStreamlined Acquisition of Control \n(1) \nThe
                requirements of [Section 6.01(a) and (b)] do not apply to a \nperson
                that has complied with and received approval to engage in money transmission
                \nunder this [Act] or was identified as a person in control in a prior
                application filed with and \napproved by the [Commissioner] or by
                an MSB accredited state pursuant to a multistate \nlicensing process,
                provided that: \n(A) \nthe person has not had a license revoked or
                suspended or \ncontrolled a licensee that has had a license revoked
                or suspended while the person \nwas in control of the licensee in
                the previous 5-years; \n(B) \nif the person is a licensee, the person
                is well managed and \nhas received at least a satisfactory rating
                for compliance at its most recent \nexamination by an MSB accredited
                state if such rating was given; \n(C) \nthe licensee to be acquired
                is projected to meet the \nrequirements of [Sections 10.01, 10.02,
                and 10.03] of this [Act] after the acquisition \nof control is completed,
                and if the person acquiring control is a licensee, that \nlicensee
                is also projected to meet the requirements of [Sections 10.01, 10.02,
                and \n10.03] of this [Act] after the acquisition of control is completed;
                \n(D) \nthe licensee to be acquired will not implement any material
                \nchanges to its business plan as a result of the acquisition of control,
                and if the person \nacquiring control is a licensee, that licensee
                also will not implement any material \nchanges to its business plan
                as a result of the acquisition of control;  and \n(E) \nthe person
                provides notice of the acquisition in cooperation \nwith the licensee
                and attests to [Section 6.01(l)(1)(A), (B), (C), and (D)] in a form
                \nand in a medium prescribed by the [Commissioner]. \n(2) \nIf the
                notice is not disapproved within 30 days after the date on \nwhich
                the notice was determined to be complete, the notice is deemed approved.
                \n(m) \nBefore filing an application for approval to acquire control
                of a licensee a \nperson may request in writing a determination from
                the [Commissioner] as to whether the person \nwould be considered
                a person in control of a licensee upon consummation of a proposed
                \ntransaction. If the [Commissioner] determines that the person would
                not be a person in control of \na licensee, the proposed Person and
                transaction is not subject to the requirements of [Section \n6.01(a)
                and (b)] of this [Act]. \n(n) \nIf a multistate licensing process
                includes a determination pursuant to \n[Section 6.01(m)] and an applicant
                avails itself or is otherwise subject to the multistate licensing
                \nprocess: \n(1) \nThe [Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged
                to accept the \ncontrol determination of a lead investigative state
                with sufficient staffing, expertise, and \nminimum standards for the
                purpose of [Section 6.01(m)]; or\n"

              is authorized and encouraged to accept the \ncontrol determination of
              a lead investigative state with sufficient staffing, expertise, and
              \nminimum standards for the purpose of [Section 6.01(m)]; or\n"

              text: "15 \n \nchecks, credit checks, fee processing, and examinations.9
                \n(d) \nThe [Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged to utilize
                NMLS forms, \nprocesses, and functionalities in accordance with this
                [Act].10 In the event NMLS does not provide \nfunctionality, forms,
                or processes for a provision of this [Act], the [Commissioner] is
                authorized \nand encouraged to strive to implement the requirements
                in a manner that facilitates uniformity \nwith respect to licensing,
                supervision, reporting, and regulation of licensees which are licensed
                in \nmultiple jurisdictions. \n(e) \nWaive or Modify Requirements.—
                For the purpose of participating in the \nNationwide Multistate Licensing
                System & Registry, the Commissioner is authorized to waive or \nmodify,
                in whole or in part, by rule, regulation or order, any or all of the
                requirements and to \nestablish new requirements as reasonably necessary
                to participate in the Nationwide Multistate \nLicensing System & Registry.
                \n[Alternative to Section 5.02(e)]: The [Commissioner] is authorized
                and encouraged to establish \nand adopt, by rule or regulation, requirements
                for participation by applicants and licensees in \nNMLS upon the [Department's]
                determination that each requirement is consistent with law, public
                \ninterest, and the purposes of this [Section 5.02].] \nSection 5.03
                Application for License. \n(a) \nApplicants for a license shall apply
                in a form and in a medium as prescribed \nby the [Commissioner]. Each
                such form shall contain content as set forth by rule, regulation,
                \ninstruction or procedure of the [Commissioner] and may be changed
                or updated by the \n[Commissioner] in accordance with applicable law
                in order to carry out the purposes of this [Act] \nand maintain consistency
                with NMLS licensing standards and practices. The application must
                state \nor contain, as applicable: \n(1) \nthe legal name and residential
                and business addresses of the \napplicant and any fictitious or trade
                name used by the applicant in conducting its business; \n(2) \na list
                of any criminal convictions of the applicant and any material \nlitigation
                in which the applicant has been involved in the [10]-year period next
                preceding \nthe submission of the application; \n(3) \na description
                of any money transmission previously provided by the \napplicant and
                the money transmission that the applicant seeks to provide in this
                state; \n \n9 Commentary: The [Commissioner] acting through its representatives
                should review and ensure that NMLS \nfunctionalities, forms, and processes
                are consistent with this Act before adopting such NMLS functionalities,
                forms, \nand processes. \n10 Commentary: The [Commissioner] acting
                through its representatives should review and ensure that NMLS \nfunctionalities,
                forms, and processes are consistent with this Act before adopting
                such NMLS functionalities, forms, \nand processes.\n"

            - unit_id: p000021

              page_number: 21

              body_hash: 5638ae03ab2c6c110a80e30639b8ccd42a1c585fdc2818a38e4f2f0fc69a5e06
              path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000021.md
              text: "21 \n \nin a medium prescribed by the [Commissioner]. The renewal
                report must state or contain a \ndescription of each material change
                in information submitted by the licensee in its original license \napplication
                which has not been reported to the [Commissioner]. \n(c) \nThe [Commissioner]
                for good cause may grant an extension of the renewal \ndate. \n(d)
                \nThe [Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged to utilize NMLS
                to \nprocess license renewals provided that such functionality is
                consistent with this [Section 5.06]. \nSection 5.07 Maintenance of
                License. \n(a) \nIf a licensee does not continue to meet the qualifications
                or satisfy the \nrequirements that apply to an applicant for a new
                money transmission license, the [Commissioner] \nmay suspend or revoke
                the licensee's license in accordance with the procedures established
                by this \n[Act] or other applicable state law for such suspension
                or revocation. \n(b) \nAn applicant for a money transmission license
                must demonstrate that it \nmeets or will meet, and a money transmission
                licensee must at all times meet, the requirements in \n[Sections 10.01,
                10.02, and 10.03] of this [Act]. \nARTICLE VI \nAcquisition of Control
                and Change of Key Individual \nSection 6.01 Acquisition of Control.
                \n(a) \nAny person, or group of persons acting in concert, seeking
                to acquire control \nof a licensee shall obtain the written approval
                of the [Commissioner] prior to acquiring control. \nAn individual
                is not deemed to acquire control of a licensee and is not subject
                to these acquisition \nof control provisions when that individual
                becomes a key individual in the ordinary course of \nbusiness. \n(b)
                \nA person, or group of persons acting in concert, seeking to acquire
                control \nof a licensee shall, in cooperation with the licensee: \n(1)
                \nSubmit an application in a form and in a medium prescribed by the
                \n[Commissioner]; and \n(2) \nSubmit a nonrefundable fee of [$X] with
                the request for approval. \n(c) \nUpon request, the [Commissioner]
                may permit a licensee or the person, or \ngroup of persons acting
                in concert, to submit some or all information required by the \n[Commissioner]
                pursuant to [Section 6.01(b)(1)] without using NMLS. \n(d) \nThe application
                required by [Section 6.01(b)(1)] shall include information \nrequired
                by [Section 5.04] for any new key individuals that have not previously
                completed the \nrequirements of [Section 5.04] for a licensee.\n"

              path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000030.md
              text: "30 \n \n(1) \nappoint the person signing the contract as the
                licensee's authorized \ndelegate with the authority to conduct money
                transmission on behalf of the licensee; \n(2) \nset forth the nature
                and scope of the relationship between the \nlicensee and the authorized
                delegate and the respective rights and responsibilities of the \nparties;
                \n(3) \nrequire the authorized delegate to agree to fully comply with
                all \napplicable state and federal laws, rules, and regulations pertaining
                to money transmission, \nincluding this [Act] and regulations implementing
                this [Act], relevant provisions of the \nBank Secrecy Act and the
                USA PATRIOT ACT; \n(4) \nrequire the authorized delegate to remit
                and handle money and \nmonetary value in accordance with the terms
                of the contract between the licensee and the \nauthorized delegate;
                \n(5) \nimpose a trust on money and monetary value net of fees received
                for \nmoney transmission for the benefit of the licensee; \n(6) \nrequire
                the authorized delegate to prepare and maintain records as \nrequired
                by this [Act] or regulations implementing this [Act], or as reasonably
                requested \nby the [Commissioner]; \n(7) \nacknowledge that the authorized
                delegate consents to examination \nor investigation by the [Commissioner];
                \n(8) \nstate that the licensee is subject to regulation by the [Commissioner]
                \nand that, as part of that regulation, the [Commissioner] may suspend
                or revoke an \nauthorized delegate designation or require the licensee
                to terminate an authorized delegate \ndesignation; and \n(9) \n(9)
                \ acknowledge receipt of the written policies and procedures \nrequired
                under [Section 8.01(b)(1)]. \n(e) \nIf the licensee's license is suspended,
                revoked, surrendered, or expired, the \nlicensee must, within five
                (5) business days, provide documentation to the [Commissioner] that
                \nthe licensee has notified all applicable authorized delegates of
                the licensee whose names are in a \nrecord filed with the [Commissioner]
                of the suspension, revocation, surrender, or expiration of a \nlicense.
                Upon suspension, revocation, surrender, or expiration of a license,
                applicable authorized \ndelegates shall immediately cease to provide
                money transmission as an authorized delegate of the \nlicensee. \n(f)
                \nAn authorized delegate of a licensee holds in trust for the benefit
                of the \nlicensee all money net of fees received from money transmission.
                \ If any authorized delegate \ncommingles any funds received from
                money transmission with any other funds or property owned \nor controlled
                by the authorized delegate, all commingled funds and other property
                shall be \nconsidered held in trust in favor of the licensee in an
                amount equal to the amount of money net of\n"

              path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000031.md
              text: "31 \n \nfees received from money transmission.22 \n(g) \nAn authorized
                delegate may not use a subdelegate to conduct money \ntransmission
                on behalf of a licensee. \nSection 8.02 Unauthorized Activities \nA
                person shall not engage in the business of money transmission on behalf
                of a person \nnot licensed under this [Act]  or not exempt pursuant
                to [Article III] of this [Act]. A person that \nengages in such activity
                provides money transmission to the same extent as if the person were
                a \nlicensee, and shall be jointly and severally liable with the unlicensed
                or nonexempt person. \nSection 8.03 [Optional]: Prohibited Authorized
                Delegates. \n(a) \nThe [appropriate court] in an action brought by
                a licensee shall have \njurisdiction to grant appropriate equitable
                or legal relief, including without limitation prohibiting \nthe authorized
                delegate from directly or indirectly acting as an authorized delegate
                for any licensee \nin this state and the payment of restitution, damages
                or other monetary relief, if the [appropriate \ncourt] finds that
                an authorized delegate failed to remit money in accordance with the
                written \ncontract required by [Section 8.01(b)] or as otherwise directed
                by the licensee or required by law. \n(b) \nIf the [appropriate court]
                issues an order prohibiting a person from acting as \nan authorized
                delegate for any licensee pursuant to [Section 8.03(a)], the licensee
                that brought the \naction shall report the order to the [Commissioner]
                within thirty (30) days and shall report the \norder through NMLS
                within ninety (90) days. \n(c) \nAn authorized delegate who holds
                money in trust for the benefit of a \nlicensee and knowingly fails
                to remit more than [$XXX] of such money is guilty of a [reference
                \nto state classification] felony. \n(d) \nAn authorized delegate
                who holds money in trust for the benefit of a \nlicensee and knowingly
                fails to remit no more than [$XXX] of such money is guilty of a [reference
                \nto state classification] misdemeanor. \nARTICLE IX  \nTimely Transmission,
                Refunds, and Disclosures \nSection 9.01 Timely Transmission. \n(a)
                \nEvery licensee shall forward all money received for transmission
                in \naccordance with the terms of the agreement between the licensee
                and the sender unless the licensee \nhas a reasonable belief or a
                reasonable basis to believe that the sender may be a victim of fraud
                or \nthat a crime or violation of law, rule, or regulation has occurred,
                is occurring, or may occur. \n(b) \nIf a licensee fails to forward
                money received for transmission in accordance \nwith this section,
                the licensee must respond to inquiries by the sender with the reason
                for the failure \n \n22 Commentary: An express trust account or segregated
                bank account is not required.\n"
